en: Ambā Stotra — Swami Vivekananda
|| Ambāstotra || Hymn to Ambā (The Mother)
Who are you, O auspicious one, who holds happiness and suffering in your hands?
Why do you repeatedly shatter this world-ocean, which is tossed by powerful waves,
in order to bring about peace here?
Therefore, O Viśvā, you are always supremely diligent.

May that Bhavānī, who accomplishes ceaselessly through her unceasing activity, and who, established as the leader of the uncreated, brings about the fruit of what has been done— may she be the granter of boons to me every day.
I know for certain this: those who hold the noose of karma are bound.
What indeed is dharma? What is it that has not been done? Where is the mark of a skull?
Or what fruit is seen here, O friend, without which the self-dependent restraints are bound by the snares of desire?
She who is the leader of this [teaching] is my refuge today.
They extend across the ocean, they conceive the net of birth and death as unchanging, yet transformed and shattered;
such are the manifestations here of her whose power is boundless.
Without relying on her, tell me, where shall we go for refuge?
O Lotus-eyed Mother, your gaze is impartial toward both friend and foe; your touch is unfailing whether one is in prosperity or distress;
your compassion is the shadow of death, yet you are also the nectar of immortality.
O you of supreme and auspicious vision, do not release me!
Where is my mother, the source of all? And where is the capacity of my dull-witted mind to grasp her— the sole sustainer of the world— within its two arms,
like one attempting to hold the venerable Śaṃkara, whose feet are meditated upon by the wise and who stands as the Lord of Fearlessness?
I take refuge in him who is praised by those for whom service is the essence.
She who dispels my birth through exceedingly painful paths by means of her own fashioned, graceful, and playful charms until its completion;
she who has constantly established my intellect upon the ground of virtue.
O Samba, my entire course of action depends upon you, whether it be fruitful or fruitless.
